findings.summary: Global item edits can silently disable tenant catalog config
findings.details: Editing a global catalog item always upserts tenant config, and when no tenantConfig is supplied it sends enabled: false. That prop is derived from a separate first-page tenant config lookup in GlobalCatalogAdminPage, so any missing config row, pagination miss, or slow/failed tenant config load turns a global item edit into a tenant-level disable/create-disabled mutation.
findings.tierReason: severity=high, confidence=0.86 (>=0.70), alreadyHandled=false — tenantConfig?.enabled ?? false defaults to false when config absent
findings.recommendation: Do not upsert tenant config from the global item form unless tenant-specific fields actually changed and the current config has been fetched for that exact item. Preserve the existing enabled value from an item-specific config fetch, and block submit or omit the config mutation when that value is unknown.

findings.summary: Concurrent approval failures leave stale actionable rows
findings.details: On a 409, the dialog closes and tells the user to refresh, but the queue query is only invalidated on mutation success. A 409 means the request was already actioned and should no longer be pending; leaving the cached row visible for the 5-minute stale window invites repeated failed approve/reject attempts.
findings.tierReason: severity=medium — does not meet blocking threshold
findings.recommendation: Invalidate or refetch ['approval-queue'] on 409/404 before closing the dialog, so the actioned row disappears immediately.

classificationRules.blockingThreshold: severity critical/high AND confidence >= 0.70 AND not alreadyHandled
classificationRules.advisoryThreshold: severity medium/low OR confidence < 0.70 OR alreadyHandled
